name: Beth Orton
label: Partisan
lede: A drama-school kid from Norfolk made a record that only came out in Japan, sang on three Chemical Brothers tracks, and spent years being filed under folktronica. Then she bought a £300 piano in Camden Market and made Weather Alive, the album Pitchfork called the best work of her career.

eras.title: Acting first, then a record only Japan got
eras.text: She trained as an actor, lost her mother at 19, and made a William Orbit record that only came out in Japan. Dancefloors heard her voice before record shops did.

years.h: Elizabeth Caroline Orton is born in Dereham, Norfolk
years.p: At fourteen she moves to Dalston, East London, and ends up at the Anna Scher Theatre School. She acts before she sings.
years.xp: Wikipedia says she did her A-levels at City College Norwich, then toured an experimental stage adaptation of Rimbaud's Une Saison en Enfer through the UK, Russia and Ukraine, playing Rimbaud's lover.

years.h: Her mother dies, and Orton leaves for Thailand
years.p: She is 19. Wikipedia says she lived for a time with Buddhist nuns.
years.xp: Wikipedia describes her mother as a journalist and political activist. Back in London, Orton worked as a waitress at Pizza Hut and briefly ran her own catering company.

years.h: Burn Blind comes out in Japan and almost nowhere else
years.p: Credited to Spill, the [[William Orbit|a7412cd0-e0b8-4fa1-8d24-75bb92a84946]] record is pressed in a tiny run. Wikipedia puts it between 1,000 and 5,000 copies.
years.xp: Orton and Orbit co-wrote every song except the John Martyn cover "Don't Wanna Know 'Bout Evil". Some didn't stay put: "She Cries Your Name" resurfaced on Trailer Park, and another track became "Montok Point" on Orbit's Strange Cargo Hinterland (1995).

years.h: Red Snapper give her one word, then a whole song
years.p: She sings a single word on [[Red Snapper|89abed31-3a93-407e-a4a3-a94e193488cd]]'s first EP, then co-writes and sings "In Deep" on The Swank EP. Their bassist Ali Friend later joins her live band.
years.xp: The one-word vocal is on "Snapper", the first Red Snapper EP, in 1994. "In Deep" came the same year.

q: And then suddenly that beat kicks in, and the entire fucking room went mental.
years.src: Irish Examiner: The entire room went mental · Wikipedia: Beth Orton
years.h: The Chemical Brothers borrow her voice for "Alive Alone"
years.p: Orton on the first time she heard it played out. Exit Planet Dust put her on dancefloors a year before Trailer Park.
years.xp:
The Irish Examiner has her at the Heavenly Social, the club night at the Albany pub in central London, where the Chemical Brothers played. Her description of the room: "60 people smushed in. It was wild."

She'd met Ed Simons and Tom Rowlands in the mid-1990s. "Where Do I Begin" (1997) and "The State We're In" (2002) followed.

eras.title: Folk songs with breakbeats underneath
eras.text: Heavenly released a folk singer who sounded like she'd been mixed in a club, and the UK took to it. Trailer Park earned a Mercury nomination, Central Reservation a second, and a Brit followed in 2000.

years.src: Wikipedia: Trailer Park (album) · Irish Examiner: The entire room went mental · Wikipedia: Beth Orton
yt: She Cries Your Name, official video
years.h: Weatherall and Van Vugt produce Trailer Park for Heavenly
years.p: Two Brit nominations and a Mercury nomination follow. Pitchfork later gave it 8.0.
years.xp:
Her first solo single, a cover of the Ronettes' "I Wish I Never Saw the Sunshine", came out in mid-1996. Wikipedia credits Orton with co-writing everything else except that cover, and says William Orbit co-wrote "She Cries Your Name". The album peaked at No. 68 in the UK and is certified Platinum there (300,000 units).

Decades later she told the Irish Examiner about Weatherall, who died in 2020 aged 56: "We made good music together."

years.h: "She Cries Your Name" gets a second go and cracks the Top 40
years.p: Re-released in June, it's her first UK Top 40 hit, arriving months after Trailer Park.

years.h: Terry Callier joins her on a Fred Neil cover
years.p: Their version of "Dolphins" on the Best Bit EP reaches No. 38 in the UK. She spends the summer on Lilith Fair.

years.src: Irish Examiner: The entire room went mental
years.h: She takes "Where Do I Begin" on Dig Your Own Hole
years.p: The Irish Examiner calls the seven-minute Chemical Brothers track the 1990s clubland answer to the Beatles' "A Day in the Life". She sings on Come with Us (2002) too.

years.src: Wikipedia: Central Reservation (album) · Wikipedia: Beth Orton
years.h: Central Reservation takes six studios and a stack of producers
years.p: [[Ben Watt|9030ae90-4db2-4a9c-aa08-01cf17a86b58]], [[Dr. Robert|8a494ebb-ed3b-43bb-bb91-e563bf2b490a]] and [[David Roback|10886c9d-c106-4337-9653-430989ec484e]] are among them; [[Terry Callier|44fd61e1-119c-479e-8301-8ac5c77148bf]] and [[Ben Harper|1582a5b8-538e-45e7-9ae4-4099439a0e79]] guest. The lead single, "Stolen Car", reaches No. 34 in the UK.
years.xp:
The album reached No. 17 in the UK and No. 110 on the Billboard 200, went Gold in the UK and earned her second Mercury nomination. The title track peaked at No. 37. Metacritic scores it 84.

Entertainment Weekly's Rob Brunner wrote that "sometimes it's enough just to let a great singer sing." Wikipedia says it appears in 1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die.

years.h: Orton takes the Brit for British female
years.p: She wins at the 2000 Brits, after two nominations for Trailer Park (newcomer and female).

eras.title: Bigger rooms, then a stripped-down record
eras.text: Daybreaker took her to No. 8 in the UK and No. 40 on the Billboard 200. Then she dropped the electronics and made Comfort of Strangers with Jim O'Rourke.

years.cap: Orton at the Prince of Wales, Melbourne
years.h: Daybreaker reaches No. 8 with Ryan Adams on guitar
years.p: It debuts at No. 40 in the US. Pitchfork gave it 4.8; Mojo called it her best to date.
years.xp:
Orton, Victor Van Vugt and [[Ben Watt|9030ae90-4db2-4a9c-aa08-01cf17a86b58]] produced, with [[Ryan Adams|c80f38a6-9980-485d-997c-5c1a9cbd0d64]] on multiple tracks and Emmylou Harris and Four Tet among the collaborators. In a July 2002 interview she said the band recorded 25 songs in two weeks, then cut the record down to ten. Recording was at Ridge Farm Studio in Surrey and Eastcote Studios.

Critics split. Metacritic's score is 70, and Q found "a crippling shortage of choruses." Wikipedia puts US sales at 169,000 as of 2003.

years.h: She closes the Daybreaker tour at a packed Royal Albert Hall
years.p: The double compilation Pass in Time follows in 2003 with B-sides, rarities, and [[William Orbit|a7412cd0-e0b8-4fa1-8d24-75bb92a84946]] and Chemical Brothers material.

years.h: Two weeks with Jim O'Rourke, and no electronics
years.p: Recorded in spring 2005 at Sear Sound in New York, with [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]] on bass, piano and marimba. Pitchfork gave it 7.2.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Orton played guitar, piano and harmonica, with Tim Barnes on drums. It peaked at No. 24 in the UK and No. 92 on the Billboard 200.

years.h: A cancelled September tour, then Nancy in December
years.p: Orton called off a September 2006 UK tour because of the pregnancy. Her daughter Nancy is born in mid-December.

eras.title: Open tunings, Portland, then synths
eras.text: After a long quiet she picked up open tunings from Bert Jansch and recorded Sugaring Season in Portland, with her husband on the record. Then Kidsticks went electronic.

years.cap: Orton at the Mojo club night, Slaughtered Lamb, Clerkenwell, London
years.h: Bert Jansch teaches her open tunings
years.p: Wikipedia says the Pentangle guitarist showed her the open guitar tunings that shape her later acoustic work. Her touring guitarist Ted Barnes and bassist Ali Friend leave to form Clayhill.

years.h: Arthur is born, and the family lives in Los Angeles until 2015
years.p: She and [[Sam Amidon|2e088ea8-b8f7-4df4-ac83-7024a50aabf1]] are married. After four years in LA they move back to London.

years.cap: Orton at NPR's Tiny Desk, August 2012
years.src: Wikipedia: Sugaring Season · Wikipedia: Beth Orton
years.h: Sugaring Season ends a six-year gap, on a new label
years.p: [[Tucker Martine|3faa4491-806c-4e7f-a6a5-a9e41135d088]] produces at his Flora studio in Portland, Oregon, with Amidon playing on it. It's her first record for ANTI-. Pitchfork gave it 7.7.
years.xp:
Announced 11 July 2012, out 1 October in the UK. Wikipedia says it was largely recorded live, with Brian Blade on drums, Rob Burger on keys and Marc Ribot on guitar. It reached No. 26 in the UK and No. 90 on the Billboard 200; Metacritic scored it 76.

Paste called it "a record that shows real artistic growth in every area."

years.h: Kidsticks turns purely electronic
years.p: Co-produced with Andrew Hung of [[Fuck Buttons|f4640b20-b76b-40d3-9ffc-a38b6718b273]], with Chris Taylor of Grizzly Bear and Twin Shadow's George Lewis Jr. Pitchfork gave it 7.6.
years.xp:
The Guardian called it a real reinvention. Wikipedia describes it as a distinct turn toward a purely electronic sound, and says she returned to Later... with Jools Holland in October 2016.

The synths didn't hide the songs on tour. John Pareles of the New York Times named her solo show that November a top gig of the year: "The songs were hypnotic, the audience silently rapt."

years.h: Spray paint on a Joshua tree sinks the "1973" video
years.p: A Change.org petition follows and the video comes down. Orton apologises.
years.xp: Wikipedia cites Billboard and Stereogum on the removal. The Mojave Desert Trust answered: "We appreciate that Beth Orton regrets her prior actions."

eras.title: A shed, a piano and a saxophone
eras.text: Six quiet years. She deals with Crohn's disease, loses Andrew Weatherall, and builds Weather Alive around a used £300 piano.

years.h: A lost Chemical Brothers cover falls out of War and Peace
years.p: The Chemical Brothers release their late-1990s cover of Tim Buckley's "I Never Asked to Be Your Mountain" with Orton. She says it fell out of an unread copy of the Tolstoy.
years.xp: Wikipedia and Mixmag both carry the story, with Orton as the source.

years.big: "I was losing words. I didn't remember the week before."
years.src: Wikipedia: Beth Orton · Uncut: Beth Orton
years.h: In The Guardian, Orton describes losing her words
years.p: She tells The Guardian about Crohn's disease and the complications from earlier medications, which affected her voice and memory.
years.xp: Wikipedia cites the interview for the quote. Uncut dates the health upheaval behind Weather Alive to a diagnosis and treatment in 2014.

years.cap: Orton at the Turning Tides Festival
q: You would play one note and about 10 would come out.
years.src: American Songwriter: Beth Orton Finds New Magic · Uncut: Beth Orton
years.h: She buys a used piano in Camden for £300 and trades in an old one
years.p: She writes the album's songs on it and records at home in London.
years.xp:
American Songwriter says the piano came from Camden Piano Rescue in Camden Market. The dealer, Desmond O'Keeffe, shipped her old Berry piano to Africa for children there. Her brief to herself: "I wanted to make a piano record. I wanted to make something really spare."

Uncut describes a battered upright in her garden shed, simple modal patterns, homemade MIDI soundscapes, and Alice Coltrane and Talk Talk as touchstones.

years.src: Album of the Year: Weather Alive · Wikipedia: Weather Alive · American Songwriter: Beth Orton Finds New Magic · Uncut: Beth Orton
years.h: Six years after Kidsticks, Weather Alive
years.p: Eight songs, self-produced from her home studio in London, with Tom Skinner, Tom Herbert, Shahzad Ismaily and Alabaster dePlume. Pitchfork's Sam Sodomsky called it the best work of her career.
years.xp:
Out 23 September 2022, her first album for Partisan after ANTI- and Decca. Album of the Year lists Pitchfork's score as 87/100 and its year-end placement at No. 23; the same page has The New York Times ranking it No. 3 and Spectrum Culture No. 1. Metacritic had it at 85 on twelve reviews, and it peaked at No. 27 in the UK. Uncut gave it 8/10.

Craig Silvey mixed it and Greg Calbi mastered it. She told American Songwriter "There's actually a part two and part three. This is just one piece of a bigger story."

years.src: The Quietus: Beth Orton Details New Album · The Vinyl Factory: Beth Orton weaves
years.h: Tom Skinner drums on it, between [[The Smile|9055fca5-69bc-4d47-b569-ab2012a19565]] and [[Sons of Kemet|fee950a2-e68c-4e76-b1ae-ff6efdf68b11]]
years.p: The Quietus and The Vinyl Factory both list him, Tom Herbert of [[The Invisible|08d43582-cee9-42a0-8ec7-bbf8389f62c2]], Ismaily and dePlume as the band.

eras.title: A Booker panel, then a second self-produced record
eras.text: She turns up on the International Booker Prize judging panel, then returns to the studio for another record she produced herself.

years.src: Irish Examiner: The entire room went mental
years.h: Orton joins the International Booker Prize judges
years.p: She's on the 2025 panel. The Irish Examiner also has her looking back on the Heavenly Social years as a very optimistic time.
years.xp: On how her work has moved, she told the Examiner: "I just quietly wanted to explore deeper the songwriting part of it. And now it's the production part of it."

years.src: The Line of Best Fit: Beth Orton announces
years.h: The Ground Above arrives, mostly captured live in the room
years.p: Self-produced again, on Partisan, with Shahzad Ismaily, Tom Herbert, Dave Okumu and others.
years.xp: The Line of Best Fit says lead single "Waiting" carries echoes of Laura Nyro, Carole King and Terry Callier. The UK headline tour runs eight dates from 12 October in Brighton to Alexandra Palace Theatre on 22 October.
